newsitem.title: UK: UK BANK SHARES EXTEND GAINS AFTER BOE RATE MOVE.
newsitem.headline: UK BANK SHARES EXTEND GAINS AFTER BOE RATE MOVE.

text.p: Shares in UK banks surged on Thursday after the Bank of England raised official base rates to 7.0 percent from 6.75 percent.
Initially bolstered by better-then-expected interim profits, shares in Barclays Plc surged 111-1/2p, or 8.4 percent, to 1439 by 1148 GMT, having scored a record at 1450p earlier.

"Banks are rate neutral - there's no impact on their profitability. The benefit comes from the perception that the Bank of England is making the right moves toward containing inflation and securing a benign environment," Morgan Stanley bank analyst Nick Collier said.
John Tyce, a bank analyst with SocGen added, "The thinking is that the economy is good, there will be fewer problems with loans and bad debts will stay low."
Shares in Standard Chartered Bank, which also posted good interim results earlier, extended its early gains, rising 32-1/2p to 1070-1/2p.
Lloyds TSB Group climbed 9-1/2p to 776-1/2, while Abbey National rose 10p to 852-1/2. Halifax Plc shares jumped 12-1/2p to 749 and shares in Banks of Scotland firmed 9-1/2p to 450.
The 11 UK banks in the FTSE 100 were contributing more than half of the 39.1-point rise in the key index, which was trading in record ground at 5,065.3.
